doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Friendship with the Nicholas Brothers
summary: Young recalls running with Fayard and Harold Nicholas, who were about his age, after sorting out their names with Brown.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Nicholas brothers, that‘s right. See, I was very good friends to the Nicholas brothers, especially the little one, he and I used to run together and everything. I learned how to dance and I‘d do dance, I wasn‘t near as good as them, the Nicholas brothers was something else, but I could dance with them. I‘d do some of the steps and things that Nicholas brothers, you hit the nail right on the head. How did you?
How did you know that? That‘s exactly what I‘m talking about, the Nicholas brothers. And the one, the two Nicholas brothers was…
Fayard. Young:…that‘s the big one, that‘s the oldest one.
And the youngest one was Maynard…
Because he was still alive, the youngest one was still along for a long time.
I think it was Fayard and um….
Fayard! Fayard. Harold Nicholas and Fayard, that‘s right, man. I used to…
We used to run together, man, we about the same age. So they, we just lost the last one…
A couple years ago we lost him.
